stories.research_notes:
Here is a fact-checked note based on available sources about the reported “first footage of pangolins captured in Huangshan Jiulongfeng Nature Reserve”:

---

## What Happened

- A monitoring team working in **Jiulongfeng Provincial Nature Reserve**, located in Huangshan City, Anhui Province, China, discovered infrared-camera footage showing a **Chinese pangolin (Manis pentadactyla, 国家一级保护野生动物, China’s first-class protected wild animal)** moving across forested terrain at night. ([ah.people.com.cn](https://ah.people.com.cn/n2/2026/1112/c374164-41749393.html?utm_source=openai))  
- This marks the **first time that this reserve has recorded Chinese pangolin activity in the wild via infrared camera**. ([ah.people.com.cn](https://ah.people.com.cn/n2/2026/1112/c374164-41749393.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## When and How

- The footage was analyzed recently, and the public report was published on **November 12, 2026**. ([ah.people.com.cn](https://ah.people.com.cn/n2/2026/1112/c374164-41749393.html?utm_source=openai))  
- The record was made as part of routine red-infrared camera monitoring by the reserve’s team, using cameras already deployed in forest areas. ([ah.people.com.cn](https://ah.people.com.cn/n2/2026/1112/c374164-41749393.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Conservation Context & Supporting Details

- Prior to this, evidence of pangolins in the Jiulongfeng area came mostly from **oral accounts** by elder local residents; there was no photographic or video evidence until this discovery. ([ah.people.com.cn](https://ah.people.com.cn/n2/2026/1112/c374164-41749393.html?utm_source=openai))  
- In the past year, a conservation data platform—“ShanSi” (山思) protection-area management system, which includes AI‐assisted screening of infrared-camera photos—processed **83,215 images** from Jiulongfeng reserve. ([ah.people.com.cn](https://ah.people.com.cn/n2/2026/1112/c374164-41749393.html?utm_source=openai))  
- The reserve has been working in cooperation with the Huangshan district government and the Tao-Huayuan Ecological Protection Foundation for several years on camera‐monitoring and patrols, as well as reducing human disturbance via guarded entrances and drone patrols. ([ah.people.com.cn](https://ah.people.com.cn/n2/2026/1112/c374164-41749393.html?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What Is *Not Yet* Known or Confirmed

- The report does *not* present data showing the pangolin population size, trend, breeding or reproduction in the reserve. There is no claim of stable or recovering population inside Jiulongfeng yet.  
- There are no published images or videos in the referenced report indicating juvenile pangolins or any breeding behavior in this reserve.  

---

## Completed Outcome vs. Plans or Claims

**Completed / Measured Outcome:**

- The successful documentation, as of November 12, 2026, of a Chinese pangolin in this reserve via infrared camera, for the first time.  
- The processing of a large dataset of infra-camera images/statistics (~83,215 photos) to enable species-identification.  

**Not a pledge, plan, or marketing claim:**

- This is *not* a mere announcement of intention; it's a concrete, documented observation.

---

## Independent Corroboration

- The primary source: People’s Daily (Anhui Channel) published the report “九龙峰自然保护区红外相机首次拍摄到中华穿山甲影像” on **November 12, 2026**, detailing the discovery. ([ah.people.com.cn](https://ah.people.com.cn/n2/2026/1112/c374164-41749393.html?utm_source=openai))  
- No other independent global English‐language outlet appears to have reported on this exact event at this time, so information is mainly from local/national Chinese sources. (However, the story aligns with broader national efforts to monitor pangolin activity via red-infrared cameras in many reserves.)  

---

## Significance & Conservation Implications

- This observation fills a documentation gap: confirming that Chinese pangolin are active in Jiulongfeng Reserve, which previously had no photographic evidence.  
- The presence of pangolin activity suggests that habitat conditions and protection efforts (e.g. patrols, anti-poaching) are sufficient, at least in part, for nocturnal, cryptic species to move about.  

---

If you like, I can look up any additional footage, images, or peer-reviewed ecological studies from the reserve to verify whether this leads toward measurable population recovery.

stories.research_notes:
Here’s a factual research note on the claim: *“Volunteers clean 160 km of coastline in Khabarovsk region.”*

---

## What actually happened

**Event:**  
Between **March and October 2026**, volunteers in Khabarovsk Krai (Russia) took part in the annual “Voda Rossii” (Water Russia) environmental campaign to clean up shores of rivers, lakes, and marine and coastal areas. ([infohabarovsk.ru](https://infohabarovsk.ru/?action=view&id=94914&module=articles&utm_source=openai))

**Measured outcome:**  
- Approximately **160 kilometers** of shoreline (including riverbanks, small rivers, lakes, and marine/coastal shores) were cleaned. ([infohabarovsk.ru](https://infohabarovsk.ru/?action=view&id=94914&module=articles&utm_source=openai))  
- About **1,000 cubic meters** of waste were collected during these cleanup operations. ([infohabarovsk.ru](https://infohabarovsk.ru/?action=view&id=94914&module=articles&utm_source=openai))  
- The efforts involved roughly **5,400 volunteers** from throughout the region. ([infohabarovsk.ru](https://infohabarovsk.ru/?action=view&id=94914&module=articles&utm_source=openai))  

**Scope and locations:**  
- Cleanup sites included river Amur, its branches and arms, smaller rivers such as Gali­chnaya and Gnilaya Pad, lakes including Hummi, Mylka, Starikovo, marine/coastal shores, and the riverbank area known as the “damn dam” (дамба) in Habarovsk. ([infohabarovsk.ru](https://infohabarovsk.ru/?action=view&id=94914&module=articles&utm_source=openai))  
- A notable event was the cleanup of the Habarovsk dam on **26 September 2026**, where ~1.5 km of shoreline was cleared (across three tiers of the dam, totaling 4.5 km when counting all levels). Over 250 volunteers participated, and several pieces of heavy equipment were used. Most of the waste there was woody debris left by floodwaters. ([news.mail.ru](https://news.mail.ru/society/73078806/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Source details and verification

- The numbers are reported by **InfoHabarovsk.ru**, citing the local Ministry of Natural Resources of Khabarovsk Krai, and also originate from ИА «Хабаровский край сегодня» (the news agency "Khabarovsk Krai Today") as primary local sources. ([infohabarovsk.ru](https://infohabarovsk.ru/?action=view&id=94914&module=articles&utm_source=openai))  
- Independent regional/regional-national media outlets (e.g. Mail.ru news, InfoHabarovsk, Губерния Онлайн) corroborate nearly all these figures. ([news.mail.ru](https://news.mail.ru/society/73078806/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Interpretation & caveats

- This event corresponds to a **completed outcome** — i.e. the cleaning was carried out over a period (March-October) and the physical measurements of coastline cleaned and waste collected are based on actual operations.  
- It’s *not* an announcement of intent or pledge; the numbers reflect what has already been done.  
- Some sources report *interim results* at earlier checkpoints (e.g., after five months: 96 km cleaned and 590 cubic meters collected) before the final total was reached. ([gubernia.com](https://gubernia.com/za-pjat-mesjacev-volontery-ochistili-ot-musora-96-kilometrov-beregov-habarovskogo-kraja/?utm_source=openai))  

---

If you like, I can check whether there’s been any detailed audit of the quality of the cleanup (e.g. types of waste, environmental impact, long-term outcomes) to see how lasting these results are.
